claims.claim: Exact harmonic duality gives a polynomial bound on fixed-width boundary signatures.
claims.evidence: Let z=y−x. Equal supplies imply equal divergence at every nonterminal. Thus regrouping Σ_e z(e)(h_t(tail(e))−h_t(head(e))) by vertices leaves x^−(t)−y^−(t), while regrouping each ordered outgoing pair gives Σ_v(d_y(v)−d_x(v))g_t(v). Because d_x,d_y∈[0,1] and |g_t(v)|≤1/2, each terminal coordinate has diameter at most Σ_v|g_t(v)|≤N/2. Fixed total terminal inflow then leaves at most (floor(N/2)+1)^(r−1) integral vectors. For φ≡1, the nonterminal transition matrix is transient in the source's absorbing setting; the displayed affine system therefore has a unique limit t≥1 for every d∈[0,1]^N, producing nonnegative edge flows with imbalance d. Choosing the two imbalance vectors according to the signs of g attains Σ_v|g(v)| for two terminals. This is a complete proof under the source's finite absorbing-graph assumptions.
claims.witness: For φ≡1, take d_y(v)=1 and d_x(v)=0 when g(v)>0, reverse these values when g(v)<0, and take them equal when g(v)=0. The resulting two flows attain terminal-inflow difference Σ_v|g(v)|.
claims.search_method: Independent directed-edge summation-by-parts derivation, transient-matrix existence argument, and exact enumeration of all 64 binary imbalance vectors for the six-nonterminal k=2 family.

claims.claim: A general range bound survives at arbitrary level width, but it can grow linearly with the number of levels.
claims.evidence: For an edge v→w, shortest-path distance satisfies d(w)≥d(v)−1. Absorption occurs almost surely, so a walk begun at level at least i reaches L_{i−1} before a sink and h at its starting vertex is the expectation of h at that first-hit point. Hence every value on L_i lies in [m_{i−1},M_{i−1}], proving the nested-range inequalities. Each successor of v∈L_i is either in L_{i−1} or at a higher level whose value is in the same interval, so |g(v)| is at most W_{i−1}/2. Summing r vertices per positive level gives the stated bound. Since W_i≤1, it is at most linear in the level count for fixed r, and the family in claim 2 realizes Θ(k) gap mass.
claims.witness: The claim-2 three-rail family has k positive levels and gap mass k(k+7)/(4(k+1))=Θ(k), so linear growth is genuinely attained rather than merely permitted by the upper bound.
claims.search_method: First-hitting-time/strong-Markov proof followed by exact checks of all level ranges and per-vertex gap inequalities for k=2,…,10 and r=3,…,6.

claims.claim: For width three, the gap mass and same-supply switching-flow diameter are unbounded; the width-two stability lemma fails already with two positive levels.
claims.evidence: The proposed graph has exactly the asserted distance levels: every vertex has a forward edge, while no edge lowers the proposed level by more than one. Substitution into the harmonic equations gives h(a_i)=i/[2(k+1)], h(b_i)=1−i/[2(k+1)], and h(c_i)=1/2. Summing the resulting gaps gives k(k+7)/[4(k+1)], which is unbounded. Claim 0's realizability argument supplies two φ≡1 switching flows attaining this entire diameter. Independently, the displayed k=2 flows satisfy nonnegativity, imbalance in {0,1}, and net outflow one at every nonterminal; their sink-1 inflows are exactly 10/3 and 11/6, differing by 3/2>1. Each padding vertex has value 1/2 and the same gap as c_i, yielding exactly k[4+(r−2)(k+3)]/[4(k+1)].
claims.witness: At k=2, use the six-vertex graph and the two listed flows. Their common supply is φ(v)=1, and their sink-1 inflow difference is 3/2, directly violating the width-two bound of one.
claims.search_method: Symbolic rational derivation plus Fraction-only verification of distances, harmonic equations, conservation, switching inequalities, directed-edge duality, padding formulas, and extremal flows in 36 cases.

claims.claim: Within-level hitting-probability order is not locally determined at width three.
claims.evidence: Both completions are directed simple graphs with precisely three vertices at each of L_1 and L_2, and they have identical sinks and identical outgoing edges from every L_1 vertex. Solving their harmonic systems exactly gives (h(a),h(b))=(3/22,1/22) in completion A and (1/22,3/22) in completion B. Thus identical information available when locally processing L_1 produces opposite strict orders. This proves failure of a rule based only on the preceding order and the current level's outgoing edges; it does not assert failure of every possible global algorithm.
claims.witness: Completion A uses X→(c,b), Y→(a,b); completion B uses X→(a,b), Y→(c,a), with common a→(0,X), b→(0,Y), c→(0,1), and Z→(a,c). The a,b order reverses exactly.
claims.search_method: Exact distance reconstruction and Fraction-valued Gaussian elimination for both six-nonterminal completions.
